notes: Desktop/floor powered studio subwoofer, not rack-mountable (omitted rackUnits). Rear panel (per Yamaha's official HS Series Owner's Manual, which includes an actual rear-panel diagram for the HS8S) has: two input channels (L and R), each with a separate balanced XLR3-31 (female) jack and a separate balanced 1/4" TRS phone jack — these are two distinct physical sockets per channel, not a single combo jack, and per Yamaha's note "the XLR and phone jack input connectors can not be used simultaneously." Two balanced male XLR3-32 output jacks (OUTPUT L, OUTPUT R) pass the (possibly low-cut-filtered) input signal through to the main L/R monitors. AC IN is a standard IEC inlet (mates with the supplied IEC C13 line cord); rear-panel drawing shows the typical 3-prong IEC C13/C14-style recessed socket, so mapped to "iec". No connector on this device belongs to a bandwidth-graded category (XLR/TRS/IEC), so no "grade" fields were set. Caveat: an older (March 2017) Yamaha "Technical Data Sheet" PDF and several retailer spec tables (echoed by web search) describe a third output, "XLR3-32 (EXT SUB)," implying 3 physical output jacks total. The current, more detailed official Owner's Manual rear-panel diagram and accompanying text ("OUTPUT L/R connectors") show only 2 physical output XLR jacks (L and R) with no separate EXT SUB jack, so I trusted the manual (with actual panel artwork) over the older datasheet's summary wording and omitted a third output port. Also note the amplifier is Class-D, 150W dynamic, and includes non-connector rear-panel controls (LEVEL, LOW CUT switch/control, HIGH CUT control, PHASE switch, power rocker switch) that are not physical I/O ports and were excluded per the task scope.
